sources.notes: Header dated January 1997. Section 10.4.3 defines 402 Payment Required as reserved for future use. Checked 2026-10-11.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics

events.title: Chaum publishes blind signatures for untraceable payments
events.detail: Year precision. David Chaum's Crypto 82 paper, printed in the 1983 proceedings, introduces blind signatures, the basis of anonymous digital cash.

events.title: Millicent proposes broker scrip for sub-cent web payments
events.detail: Month precision (WWW4, Boston). Digital Equipment Corporation researchers describe vendor-specific scrip validated by the vendor's own server, aimed at purchases under one cent. A companion paper appeared at the First USENIX Workshop on Electronic Commerce in July 1995.

events.title: Rivest and Shamir present PayWord and MicroMint
events.detail: Month precision. Presented at the Security Protocols workshop in Cambridge, UK, in April 1996 and published in LNCS 1189 in 1997 (DOI 10.1007/3-540-62494-5_6). PayWord uses hash chains for repeated small payments to one vendor.

events.title: HTTP/1.1 (RFC 2068) reserves 402 Payment Required for future use
events.detail: Month precision (January 1997). Section 10.4.3 names the status code and reserves it without defining a payment mechanism.

events.title: Rivest proposes electronic lottery tickets as micropayments
events.detail: Month precision (Financial Cryptography 1997, Anguilla). Probabilistic payments let a payer send a ticket that pays a larger amount with small probability, cutting per-payment processing cost.

events.title: RFC 2616 keeps 402 reserved
events.detail: Month precision (June 1999). RFC 2616 obsoletes RFC 2068 and keeps 402 Payment Required reserved for future use.

events.title: Macaroons introduce attenuable bearer credentials with caveats
events.detail: Month precision (NDSS 2014). Google and academic authors describe chained-HMAC tokens that holders can restrict with caveats. L402 later uses macaroons as its credential format.

events.title: EMVCo publishes the Payment Tokenisation Specification Technical Framework v1.0
events.detail: Network tokens replace the card number with a token restricted to a device, merchant or channel. Card-network agent schemes build on this token model. Date from a trade press report; the EMVCo library page was not confirmed directly.

events.title: Lightning Network white paper draft 0.5.9.2
events.detail: Joseph Poon and Thaddeus Dryja describe payment channels for off-chain bitcoin payments. This dated draft followed earlier 2015 versions.

events.title: Lightning Labs announces LSAT for paid APIs over HTTP 402
events.detail: LSAT combines a macaroon credential with a Lightning invoice returned on a 402 response. Aperture, a reverse proxy, implements it.

events.title: RFC 9110 consolidates HTTP semantics and still reserves 402
events.detail: Month precision (June 2022). Section 15.5.3 keeps 402 (Payment Required) reserved for future use.

events.title: Lightning Labs renames LSAT to L402 in its specification
events.detail: A documentation rewrite in the lightninglabs/L402 repository (commit d31479c) replaces LSAT with L402; servers and clients keep accepting both scheme names. Lightning Labs used the L402 name publicly in its 2023-07-06 AI agent tooling announcement.

events.title: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures and RFC 9530 Digest Fields published
events.detail: Month precision (February 2024). Both are Standards Track. Visa TAP and other agent schemes sign HTTP requests with RFC 9421.
